hero.subtitle: From its Spanish founding to becoming a UNESCO World Heritage Site, discover the moments that shaped Cartagena's identity.

timeline.title: Interactive timeline
timeline.subtitle: Journey through the most important moments in Cartagena's history.

founding.title: Founding of Cartagena
founding.subtitle: Pedro de Heredia establishes the city
founding.description: Spanish conquistador Pedro de Heredia founds Cartagena de Indias on June 1, 1533, establishing one of the most important ports in the New World. The city quickly becomes the main gateway for wealth flowing to and from Spain.
founding.fact1: First major city founded on Colombia's Caribbean coast

walls.title: Building the city walls
walls.subtitle: Fortifications against pirates and enemy fleets
walls.description: Over more than 150 years, the imposing walls surrounding the city are built. Designed by Spanish military engineers, these fortifications protect Cartagena from constant attacks by pirates, privateers and enemy fleets.

siege1741.title: Siege of Cartagena
siege1741.subtitle: Heroic victory against the British fleet
siege1741.description: The city heroically withstands the siege of the British fleet commanded by Admiral Edward Vernon. Spanish Admiral Blas de Lezo successfully defends the city in one of the largest naval battles in the colonial history of the Americas.
siege1741.fact2: Blas de Lezo, hero of the defense
siege1741.fact3: Victory that shaped the colonial balance of power

independence.title: Independence - Heroic City
independence.subtitle: First to declare full independence
independence.description: Cartagena becomes the first city in present-day Colombia to declare absolute independence from Spain on November 11, 1811. This bold act earns it the title of "Heroic City" and sparks the independence movement across the region.
independence.fact3: Cradle of liberty in the Americas

morillo.title: Morillo's siege and the Reconquest
morillo.subtitle: Resistance during the Spanish Reconquest
morillo.description: Pablo Morillo besieges the city for 106 days. The population resists heroically until hunger and disease force a surrender. Thousands of residents die defending their freedom, cementing the city's heroic spirit.

unesco.title: World Heritage Site
unesco.subtitle: UNESCO global recognition
unesco.description: UNESCO declares the historic center of Cartagena a Cultural World Heritage Site, recognizing its outstanding universal value. Its walls, fortifications and colonial architecture are preserved for future generations.
